learner_operation: Identify a distinct parallel line by isolating y in a given standard-form equation and matching slopes among complete line choices. In hard, compare normalized intercepts to reject coincidence after matching slopes.

fixed_features.feature: Five complete line-equation choices and one correct radio selection
fixed_features.justification: Four complete imported questions use this contract. Keeping one unique answer avoids adding subset selection or unknown-parameter algebra.

fixed_features.feature: Nonvertical, nonhorizontal lines with small nonzero signed integer/familiar rational slopes
fixed_features.justification: Isolation of y and slope comparison are the assessed operation. Vertical lines require a separate classification; zero slopes remove the x-term rearrangement. The restricted magnitude holds prerequisite arithmetic manageable, without fixing sign or target.

fixed_features.feature: Hard includes two equal-slope pairs and one singleton; target belongs to a pair
fixed_features.justification: A coincident candidate makes intercept comparison necessary. The second wrong-slope pair prevents a unique repeated slope from identifying the target. The singleton cannot assess coincidence. Four candidates can exchange the keyed role in the same fixed bank.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: All five candidates in easy/moderate; either member of either equal-slope pair in hard. Position, slope sign/rank, equation scale and intercept are not fixed.
answer_roles.observed: Each final raw/delivered batch keys each of the five stored positions once. First easy/moderate bank cycles through all five targets; first hard bank through four eligible targets. Fresh controls cover both signs, integer/fractional slopes and every position.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Slope chooses eligible target; constant may vary without changing easy/moderate target. In hard, the given intercept chooses which member of the target slope pair coincides.
answer_roles.observed: Controlled fixed-bank pairs change the target slope in easy/moderate and swap coincident/correct roles in hard; all resulting keys, solutions, rendered prompts and learner outcomes change correctly.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Distinct unequal-slope lines in easy/moderate. Hard also includes the same geometric line and another wrong equal-slope pair. Every line uses the same response formatting.
answer_roles.observed: All five options checked per question; wrong choices fail the independent slope/distinctness criterion and native grader. Their error is accepting an unequal slope or accepting coincidence on slope alone, as appropriate.

coverage.case: Final easy, moderate and hard batches plus actual delivered survivors
coverage.result: All 15 pass independently. No duplicates against basis 8004; all 15 remain delivered. Each batch uses every raw position and multiple answers. Easy integral slopes, moderate three integral/two rational, hard four integral/one rational; both signs in each band.

coverage.case: Independent fresh-seed sample 90731/90732/90733, count 24 per band
coverage.result: Every target position and both signs observed; moderate 13/24 fractional and hard 4/24 fractional. Hard fresh sample has no zero given intercept, but the exact final hard batch supplies that boundary. No claim that random controls exhaust the finite parameter domain.

coverage.case: Fixed bank answer-role reassignment and scaling
coverage.result: Relevant changes reverse the correct candidate; irrelevant scaling preserves its mathematical equation. Actual grader checks every choice; rendered controls/prompts and explanations match the changed records.

counterfactuals.change: Keep all five candidate equations fixed and change given slope for easy/moderate; keep given slope but swap which paired intercept is coincident in hard.
counterfactuals.expected: Correct geometric choice changes; given equation, solution and selection outcomes follow the target.
counterfactuals.observed: All three pairs changed winner as independently derived; both members render fully and every native response outcome follows the changed criterion.
counterfactuals.justification: Slope/intercept evidence determines the relationship; a particular source qualifying line is incidental.

counterfactuals.change: Multiply the given equation by -3, preserving candidate bank and geometric line.
counterfactuals.expected: The correct mathematical equation remains the same; solution normalizes changed coefficients.
counterfactuals.observed: All three scaled controls preserve the winner, update given/isolation rows and pass native grading and actual UI formula checks. IDs may change with content; the geometric choice is preserved.
counterfactuals.justification: Multiplying a line equation by a nonzero scalar preserves both slope and intercept.

learner fresh/usable filtering and weighted selection source plus faithful read-only reproduction

delivery.result: All 87 final/control input records survive the actual filter at captured basis 8004 with target/visible content preserved. No declared bank-only probe perfectly answers any tested full band or control subgroup; actual UI shuffle also has no tested perfect predictor in any five-item final pool. Selection weights contain no target/key criterion; histories exclude exact previously seen records. All eligible records remain reachable with positive configured weight. Unconfigured first-ID fallback and hypothetical history depletion are explicitly limited in learner-selection.json.

limitations: Finite tests cannot prove absence of all shortcuts; the strategies declare their allowed information and compare with 0.2 uniform selection.

Small final pools have incidental partial position correlations after UI shuffle (e.g. 3/5), but no tested universal answer rule. Tested fixed-bank controls demonstrate that the bank alone cannot determine its correct member.

Hard bank geometry legitimately excludes the singleton and narrows targets to two pairs; this mathematical inference cannot identify one winner and is intrinsic to ensuring coincidence work. Original complete source banks do not contain coincident alternatives; this extension is justified by the lesson distinctness definition.

Learner selection uses surrogate IDs in a faithful reproduction; actual future DB identities, learner histories and configured weights are unavailable. All bands are separately verified, not certified as published.
Only easy has imported difficulty labels. Higher bands are a documented authored progression, without empirical learner calibration.
